issues.display_title: Issue #521: Refactor Broadcast Module and Centralize Notification Helpers
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor Broadcast Module and Centralize Notification Helpers

Summary

Refactored src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ by extracting shared authorization checks, post payload construction, web/mobile token parsers, and bookmark aggregation logic into broadcast_helpers.go. Integrated the helpers into AddPostSubscribe.go, PickOfTheDay.go, and RemoveAllBroadcast.go, and established a comprehensive unit test suite in broadcast_helpers_test.go.

Files Updated

1. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/broadcast_helpers.go

  • FolderBookmark & FolderBookmarkRow: Extracted shared models for bookmark folder grouping and database row scanning.
  • GetAccountSP() string: Safe retrieval of super admin configuration from ACCOUNT_SP env or package fallback.
  • IsSuperAdmin(email, accountSPConfig string) bool: Checks super admin access with empty checks.
  • ValidateBroadcastRole(role string) bool: Validates user or support role for broadcast removal.
  • IsPostPublic(visibility *string) bool: Helper to check if visibility pointer is "public".
  • ResolvePostSubscribeSidQuery(sl string, pw *bool) string: Query resolver for AddPostSubscribe (id vs slug).
  • ResolvePickOfTheDaySidQuery(sl string, pw *bool) string: Query resolver for PickOfTheDay (id vs slug).
  • BuildBroadcastPostPayload(post Models.Post) map[string]interface{}: Unified post payload builder including unescaping HTML descriptions and wrapping long/short descriptions.
  • BuildPostImagePath(post Models.Post, baseImgURL string) (string, string): Returns image URL and slug path.
  • FormatNotificationBody(template, name string) string: Replaces [name] placeholder with user fullname.
  • ParseWebNotificationTokens(checkNotifWeb []Models.NotificationsWeb) ([][]Models.NotificationWeb, error): Parses and chunks web notification tokens into batches of 10.
  • ExtractMobileTokens(notifications []Models.PushNotification, chunkSize int) [][]string: Flattens and chunks mobile tokens (default chunk size: 100).
  • GroupFolderBookmarks(results []FolderBookmarkRow) ([]FolderBookmark, error): Aggregates database rows into ordered FolderBookmark slices while ensuring public visibility.
  • GenerateBroadcastSlug(now time.Time) string: Generates unique random hex and timestamped slugs.
  • BuildBookmarkBroadcastData(fb FolderBookmark, slug, titleSend, bodySend string) map[string]interface{}: Formats broadcast data payload for bookmark notifications.
  • GetFolderBookmarkImage(fb FolderBookmark, baseImgURL string) string: Extracts thumbnail URL from folder bookmarks.
  • BuildAddPostContainerDatas(...): Assembles datas and vDatas maps for broadcast containers.

2. src/Action/V1/Broadcast/broadcast_helpers_test.go

  • Implemented 15 comprehensive unit tests using standard library testing:
    • TestGetAccountSP: Tests env retrieval and fallback.
    • TestIsSuperAdmin: Table-driven tests for matching, not found, and empty inputs.
    • TestValidateBroadcastRole: Validates user and support roles against invalid roles.
    • TestIsPostPublic: Checks public, private, unlisted, and nil visibility.
    • TestResolvePostSubscribeSidQuery: Tests sl and pw query resolution variations.
    • TestResolvePickOfTheDaySidQuery: Tests sl and pw query resolution variations.
    • TestBuildBroadcastPostPayload: Verifies slug, description unescaping, and wrap texts.
    • TestBuildPostImagePath: Tests thumbnail and non-thumbnail image/path assembly.
    • TestFormatNotificationBody: Tests [name] replacement.
    • TestParseWebNotificationTokens: Tests empty, valid tokens, and invalid JSON error handling.
    • TestExtractMobileTokens: Tests chunking and empty token filtering.
    • TestGroupFolderBookmarks: Tests row grouping, multiple bookmarks, and non-public visibility rejection.
    • TestGenerateBroadcastSlug: Tests slug format and timestamp inclusion.
    • TestBuildBookmarkBroadcastData: Tests payload formatting and unescaping bookmark name.
    • TestGetFolderBookmarkImage: Tests thumbnail extraction with and without bookmarks.
    • TestBuildAddPostContainerDatas: Tests structure and values of container payload.

3. Handlers in src/Action/V1/Broadcast/

  • AddPostSubscribe.go:
    • Replaced inline query resolution with ResolvePostSubscribeSidQuery.
    • Replaced inline visibility check with IsPostPublic.
    • Replaced inline image/path formatting with BuildPostImagePath.
    • Replaced string replacement with FormatNotificationBody.
    • Replaced duplicate buildPostSubscribePayload with BuildBroadcastPostPayload.
    • Replaced web token loop with ParseWebNotificationTokens.
    • Replaced container maps with BuildAddPostContainerDatas.
    • Protected Fiber locals (role, userId, encrypt) with safe type assertions.
  • PickOfTheDay.go:
    • Replaced inline query resolution with ResolvePickOfTheDaySidQuery.
    • Replaced inline visibility checks with IsPostPublic.
    • Replaced duplicate buildPickOfTheDayPostPayload with BuildBroadcastPostPayload.
    • Replaced inline bookmark grouping with GroupFolderBookmarks.
    • Replaced mobile and web token chunking with ExtractMobileTokens and ParseWebNotificationTokens.
    • Replaced slug generation with GenerateBroadcastSlug.
    • Replaced super admin checks with IsSuperAdmin(..., GetAccountSP()).
    • Removed duplicate FolderBookmark struct and accountSP package variable.
  • RemoveAllBroadcast.go:
    • Replaced role validation with ValidateBroadcastRole.
    • Replaced super admin check with IsSuperAdmin(..., GetAccountSP()).
    • Added safe type assertions for Fiber locals and map lookups.

Verification

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast/...
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast
go test ./...
  • All unit tests in src/Action/V1/Broadcast passed.
  • go vet reported zero issues.
  • Entire project test suite across all packages passed cleanly.

Problem

The src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ package contained three action files (AddPostSubscribe.go, PickOfTheDay.go, and RemoveAllBroadcast.go) with duplicated code patterns and zero unit tests:

  1. Duplicated Post Payload Construction: AddPostSubscribe.go and PickOfTheDay.go maintained separate but identical post payload builder functions (buildPostSubscribePayload and buildPickOfTheDayPostPayload) and repeated post description unescaping and text wrapping.
  2. Duplicated Web & Mobile Token Parsing: Parsing, chunking, and unmarshaling of web notification tokens (NotificationsWeb) was implemented identically in both AddPostSubscribe.go and PickOfTheDay.go.
  3. Duplicated Super Admin and Role Checks: Super admin verification (strings.Contains(accountSP, email)) and role checks were repeated with unsafe type assertions on context locals that risked runtime panics.
  4. Duplicated Post Visibility & Path Generation: Repetitive checks for post public visibility and post image/path construction across broadcast actions.
  5. Zero Test Coverage: The src/Action/V1/Broadcast package had no unit test suite.

Scope

  • Create src/Action/V1/Broadcast/broadcast_helpers.go:
    • FolderBookmark & FolderBookmarkRow: Extracted models for bookmark grouping.
    • GetAccountSP: Retrieves the configured super admin account list with fallback.
    • IsSuperAdmin: Validates whether an email has super admin authorization.
    • ValidateBroadcastRole: Validates whether the caller role is authorized for broadcast removal.
    • IsPostPublic: Checks if the post has public visibility.
    • ResolvePostSubscribeSidQuery: Resolves the query identifier condition for post subscriptions.
    • ResolvePickOfTheDaySidQuery: Resolves the query identifier condition for pick of the day.
    • BuildBroadcastPostPayload: Unified constructor for post broadcast payload with description unescaping and wrapping.
    • BuildPostImagePath: Constructs the image URL and path for posts.
    • FormatNotificationBody: Interpolates the sender's full name into body templates.
    • ParseWebNotificationTokens: Safely unmarshals and chunks web notification tokens.
    • ExtractMobileTokens: Gathers and chunks mobile notification tokens.
    • GroupFolderBookmarks: Aggregates flat database rows into structured folder bookmarks while enforcing public visibility.
    • GenerateBroadcastSlug: Generates timestamped random broadcast slugs.
    • BuildBookmarkBroadcastData: Assembles the broadcast payload for bookmark folders.
    • GetFolderBookmarkImage: Resolves thumbnail URL from folder bookmarks.
    • BuildAddPostContainerDatas: Constructs datas and vDatas maps for broadcast containers.
  • Refactor AddPostSubscribe.go, PickOfTheDay.go, and RemoveAllBroadcast.go to use the centralized helpers and panic-safe type assertions.
  • Create comprehensive unit test suite in src/Action/V1/Broadcast/broadcast_helpers_test.go.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% backward compatible: No changes to API routes, request/response formats, database queries, or notification dispatch contracts.

Acceptance Criteria

  • broadcast_helpers.go implemented and used across all Broadcast handlers.
  • broadcast_helpers_test.go implemented and passing with high coverage.
  • All tests in src/Action/V1/Broadcast/... pass (go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast).
  • go vet ./src/Action/V1/Broadcast reports zero issues.
  • Full test suite across codebase passes (go test ./...).

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-30.

issues.display_title: Issue #522: Refactor Register Module and Centralize Registration Helpers
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor Register Module and Centralize Registration Helpers

Summary

Refactored src/Action/V1/Register/ by extracting shared model constructors (User, UserAccount, Otp), username/fullname sanitizers, linked account detectors, registration payload builders, OAuth avatar processor, and encryption responders into register_helpers.go. Integrated the helpers across ValidateRegister.go, RegisterUser.go, RegisterGoogle.go, and RegisterApple.go, and created a comprehensive unit test suite in register_helpers_test.go.

Files Updated

1. src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers.go

  • IsValidRegistrationType(t string) bool: Validates registration type query (register, google, apple, keycloak).
  • SanitizeRegistrationUsername(username string) string: Normalizes username (replaces . with _, removes ', appends a to purely numeric usernames, converts to lowercase).
  • SanitizeOAuthFullname(name string) string: Strips numbers and title-cases name words.
  • ResolveUsernameCollision(username string, randInt int) string: Appends random integer to usernames on collision.
  • BuildNewUserModel(...) Models.User: Unified constructor for Models.User instances with optional password, country, avatar, and path.
  • BuildUserAccountModel(...) Models.UserAccount: Unified constructor for Models.UserAccount supporting google, apple, or standard registrations.
  • BuildOtpModel(...) Models.Otp: Constructor for email verification OTP records.
  • BuildEmailVerificationPayload(...) map[string]interface{}: Formats email verification RabbitMQ message payload.
  • DetectLinkedAccountProvider(...) string: Determines whether an email is already associated with Google, Facebook, or Apple account.
  • BuildRegistrationResponse(...) map[string]interface{}: Generates registration success payload supporting slim OTP output.
  • BuildAvatarFilename(now time.Time, randomHex string) string: Generates timestamped random-hex avatar filename.
  • RespondOAuthRegistration(...) error: Encapsulates plain and AES/custom encrypted OAuth registration responses.
  • processOAuthAvatar(...) (string, string, error): Encapsulates downloading avatar from URL, determining dimensions, uploading to MinIO, and signing with imgproxy.

2. src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers_test.go

  • Implemented 12 unit tests using standard library testing:
    • TestIsValidRegistrationType: Tests valid and invalid registration types.
    • TestSanitizeRegistrationUsername: Tests dots to underscore, quote removal, numeric suffixing, and lowercasing.
    • TestSanitizeOAuthFullname: Tests digit removal and title-casing.
    • TestResolveUsernameCollision: Tests collision integer appending.
    • TestBuildNewUserModel: Validates proper field assignment on Models.User.
    • TestBuildUserAccountModel: Validates Google, Apple, and standard user account building.
    • TestBuildOtpModel: Validates verification code and expiration fields.
    • TestBuildEmailVerificationPayload: Validates RabbitMQ payload structure.
    • TestDetectLinkedAccountProvider: Tests Google, Facebook, Apple, and no-match cases.
    • TestBuildRegistrationResponse: Tests standard and slim OTP responses.
    • TestBuildAvatarFilename: Tests timestamp and .jpg extension formatting.
    • TestRespondOAuthRegistration: Tests plain and encrypted response generation.

3. Handlers in src/Action/V1/Register/

  • ValidateRegister.go:
    • Replaced manual registration type validation with IsValidRegistrationType.
    • Replaced manual username sanitization with SanitizeRegistrationUsername.
    • Safe type assertions for user map entries (is_email_verified, id).
  • RegisterUser.go:
    • Replaced manual linked account checks with DetectLinkedAccountProvider.
    • Replaced manual Models.User construction with BuildNewUserModel.
    • Replaced manual Models.UserAccount construction with BuildUserAccountModel.
    • Replaced manual Models.Otp construction with BuildOtpModel.
    • Replaced manual verification queue message construction with BuildEmailVerificationPayload.
    • Replaced manual registration response map with BuildRegistrationResponse.
  • RegisterGoogle.go:
    • Replaced manual fullname cleaning with SanitizeOAuthFullname.
    • Replaced collision integer concatenation with ResolveUsernameCollision.
    • Replaced Models.User and Models.UserAccount construction with BuildNewUserModel and BuildUserAccountModel.
    • Replaced deep-nested encryption output with RespondOAuthRegistration.
    • Moved processOAuthAvatar to register_helpers.go.
  • RegisterApple.go:
    • Replaced manual fullname cleaning with SanitizeOAuthFullname.
    • Replaced collision integer concatenation with ResolveUsernameCollision.
    • Replaced Models.User and Models.UserAccount construction with BuildNewUserModel and BuildUserAccountModel.

Verification

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Register/...
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Register
go test ./...
  • All unit tests in src/Action/V1/Register passed.
  • go vet reported 0 issues.
  • All test suites across the repository passed cleanly.

Problem

The src/Action/V1/Register/ package contains four action files (RegisterUser.go, RegisterGoogle.go, RegisterApple.go, and ValidateRegister.go) totaling over 800 lines of code with zero unit test coverage:

  1. Duplicated Model Construction: Identical creation logic for Models.User, Models.UserAccount, and Models.Otp across standard registration and OAuth registration handlers.
  2. Duplicated Username & Fullname Sanitization: Logic for stripping dots, quotes, digits, converting case, and resolving username collisions is repeated across handlers.
  3. Duplicated Account Linking & Verification Messages: Detection of existing linked accounts (Google, Facebook, Apple) and email verification queue payload creation are duplicated or scattered.
  4. Duplicated Response Formatting: Response construction (plain, slim OTP, and encrypted AES/custom encryption) is handled manually with deep nesting.
  5. Zero Test Coverage: The src/Action/V1/Register package currently has no unit tests.

Scope

  • Create src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers.go:
    • IsValidRegistrationType: Validates the registration type (register, google, apple, keycloak).
    • SanitizeRegistrationUsername: Cleans and normalizes usernames (dots to underscore, remove quotes, prevent pure numeric).
    • SanitizeOAuthFullname: Removes numbers and applies title-casing to names.
    • ResolveUsernameCollision: Appends random integers when OAuth usernames collide.
    • BuildNewUserModel: Unified constructor for Models.User.
    • BuildUserAccountModel: Unified constructor for Models.UserAccount supporting providers (google, apple, or standard).
    • BuildOtpModel: Constructor for Models.Otp verification codes.
    • BuildEmailVerificationPayload: Assembles RabbitMQ email verification queue message.
    • DetectLinkedAccountProvider: Identifies existing linked accounts from user_account row.
    • BuildRegistrationResponse: Standard response constructor for user registration with slim OTP support.
    • RespondOAuthRegistration: Response helper for OAuth registration supporting encrypted payloads (ec and sl).
    • BuildAvatarFilename: Generates timestamped and random hex filenames for avatars.
    • processOAuthAvatar: Encapsulated avatar download, dimension extraction, MinIO upload, and imgproxy URL generation.
  • Refactor ValidateRegister.go, RegisterUser.go, RegisterGoogle.go, and RegisterApple.go to use the helpers.
  • Create unit tests in src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers_test.go.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% backward compatible: No breaking changes to endpoints (/api/v1/register/*), validation error messages, or token formats.

Acceptance Criteria

  • register_helpers.go implemented and integrated into all Register handlers.
  • register_helpers_test.go implemented with comprehensive unit tests.
  • All tests in src/Action/V1/Register/... pass (go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Register).
  • go vet ./src/Action/V1/Register reports zero issues.
  • Entire test suite across codebase passes (go test ./...).

Delivery

issues.display_title: Issue #523: Refactor Auth Login Module and Centralize Login Helpers
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor Auth Login Module and Centralize Login Helpers

Summary

Refactored src/Action/V1/Auth/ by centralizing database user row parsing into ParsedLoginUser with panic-safe extractions, extracting standardized responses for unregistered and unverified users, consolidating OTP upsert and email verification message creation, and cleaning up JWT claim builders for viewer login and address search tokens.

Files Updated

1. src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers.go

  • ParsedLoginUser: Type-safe struct holding typed fields (ID, Encrypt, Fullname, Email, Username, UserReqDelete, IsActive, IsBack, IsEmailVerified, IsPassword, IsEmail) safely extracted from database query maps.
  • ParseLoginUserData(userDatas map[string]interface{}) ParsedLoginUser: Panic-safe parser handling nil maps, null values, and type assertions.
  • BuildUnregisteredResponse(isSlim bool) (int, map[string]interface{}): Unified generator for unregistered account response, handling HTTP 200 (slim) vs 400 status.
  • BuildUnverifiedResponse(customMessage ...string) (int, map[string]interface{}): Unified generator for unverified account response (HTTP 400).
  • BuildUnverifiedEmailLoginResponse(jwtString string) (int, map[string]interface{}): Formats HTTP 403 Forbidden payload containing registration JWT token.
  • BuildViewerHasuraClaims(exp int64, isEncrypted bool) map[string]interface{}: Constructs claims for viewer JWT tokens.
  • BuildTokenSearchAddressClaims(now time.Time, duration time.Duration) map[string]interface{}: Constructs claims for address search tokens.
  • BuildEmailVerificationPayload(email, fullname string, otpCode int) map[string]interface{}: Builds RabbitMQ email verification queue payload.
  • UpsertEmailVerificationOtp(...) error: Upserts OTP records in CockroachDB for unverified login flow.

2. src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers_test.go

  • Added comprehensive unit tests:
    • TestParseLoginUserData: Validates nil input, full data parsing, and boolean flags.
    • TestBuildUnregisteredResponse: Validates slim vs standard status codes and payloads.
    • TestBuildUnverifiedResponse: Validates default and custom message handling.
    • TestBuildUnverifiedEmailLoginResponse: Validates 403 status and token inclusion.
    • TestBuildViewerHasuraClaims: Validates claims with and without expiration.
    • TestBuildTokenSearchAddressClaims: Validates issued-at and expiration timestamps.
    • TestBuildEmailVerificationPayloadInAuth: Validates queue message format.

3. Handlers in src/Action/V1/Auth/

  • Login.go:
    • Replaced unsafe type assertions with ParseLoginUserData.
    • Replaced procedural OTP query/create/update with UpsertEmailVerificationOtp.
    • Replaced inline RabbitMQ payload with BuildEmailVerificationPayload.
    • Replaced unverified login response with BuildUnverifiedEmailLoginResponse.
  • LoginGoogle.go:
    • Replaced duplicated unregistered response with BuildUnregisteredResponse.
    • Replaced duplicated unverified response with BuildUnverifiedResponse.
    • Replaced unsafe assertions with ParseLoginUserData.
  • LoginApple.go:
    • Replaced duplicated unregistered response with BuildUnregisteredResponse.
    • Replaced duplicated unverified responses in both LoginApple and LoginAppleAfterRegister with BuildUnverifiedResponse.
    • Replaced unsafe assertions with ParseLoginUserData.
  • LoginViewer.go:
    • Removed stale package-level lastLogin global variable; timestamp is now generated dynamically per request.
    • Replaced raw claims map with BuildViewerHasuraClaims.
  • TokenSearchAddress.go:
    • Replaced raw claims map with BuildTokenSearchAddressClaims.

Verification

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Auth/...
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Auth
go test ./...
  • All 22 unit tests in src/Action/V1/Auth passed.
  • go vet reported zero issues.
  • Entire project test suite across all packages passed cleanly.

Problem

The login handlers in src/Action/V1/Auth/ (Login.go, LoginGoogle.go, LoginApple.go, LoginViewer.go, and TokenSearchAddress.go) exhibit common issues:

  1. Unsafe Type Assertions: Handlers extract fields from database row maps via direct assertions (userDatas["id"].(string), userDatas["is_email_verified"].(bool)), risking runtime panics if fields are missing or NULL.
  2. Duplicated Response Constructors:
    • Unregistered user responses ("Please Register First", with slim-mode status code handling) are duplicated across LoginGoogle.go and LoginApple.go.
    • Unverified account responses ("Verified your account" / "Verify your account") are duplicated across LoginGoogle.go, LoginApple.go, and LoginAppleAfterRegister.
  3. Procedural OTP & Verification Handling: Login.go contains procedural database querying, branching, and model upserting for OTP tokens when an email is unverified.
  4. Static Initialization in Viewer Login: LoginViewer.go uses a package-level lastLogin variable initialized at server startup rather than dynamic invocation time.
  5. Claims Construction: Hasura viewer claims and address search token claims are constructed manually with raw maps.

Scope

  • Extend src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers.go:
    • ParsedLoginUser: Safe struct representation of user row data.
    • ParseLoginUserData: Safe parser for map[string]interface{} without panic risks.
    • BuildUnregisteredResponse: Standardized unregistered response generator with slim status logic.
    • BuildUnverifiedResponse: Standardized unverified response generator.
    • BuildUnverifiedEmailLoginResponse: 403 response for unverified email login with token.
    • BuildViewerHasuraClaims: JWT claims constructor for viewer login.
    • BuildTokenSearchAddressClaims: JWT claims constructor for address search tokens.
    • UpsertEmailVerificationOtp: Database helper to insert or update email verification OTP.
    • BuildEmailVerificationPayload: RabbitMQ email verification queue message builder.
  • Refactor Login.go, LoginGoogle.go, LoginApple.go, LoginViewer.go, and TokenSearchAddress.go to use these helpers.
  • Expand helpers_test.go with unit tests for all new helper functions.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% backward compatible: No changes to endpoint contracts, status codes, JWT claims structure, or response payloads.

Acceptance Criteria

  • helpers.go updated and integrated across all login actions.
  • helpers_test.go updated with unit test coverage.
  • All tests in src/Action/V1/Auth/... pass (go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Auth).
  • go vet ./src/Action/V1/Auth reports zero issues.
  • Entire project test suite passes (go test ./...).

issues.display_title: Issue #524: Embed Keycloak Refresh Token in JWT Claims and Extract During Logout
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Embed Keycloak Refresh Token in JWT Claims and Extract During Logout

Summary

Implemented automatic Keycloak SSO session termination by embedding the Keycloak refresh_token inside the Panorra Hasura JWT payload during Keycloak login. During logout, if refresh_token is not explicitly provided in the request body or query, it is automatically extracted from the JWT token (via Authorization header, Fiber locals, or body token) to terminate the Keycloak SSO session.

Files Updated

1. src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers.go

  • BuildKeycloakJWTPayload(userId, encrypt string, now time.Time, refreshToken string) map[string]interface{}:
    • Builds Hasura JWT claims and adds "keycloak": {"refresh_token": refreshToken} when provided.
  • ExtractRefreshTokenFromClaim(claim interface{}) string:
    • Safely extracts the refresh token from either map[string]interface{} ({"refresh_token": "..."}) or direct string.
  • ExtractKeycloakRefreshToken(c *fiber.Ctx, bodyRefreshToken, bodyToken string) string:
    • Cascading extraction from body refresh_token, query refresh_token, c.Locals("keycloak"), Authorization: Bearer <JWT>, and body/query token.

2. src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakHandlers.go

  • keycloakLoginBody: Added RefreshToken string json:"refresh_token".
  • authenticateKeycloak: Extracts requestBody.RefreshToken (with query fallback) and passes to respondKeycloakLogin.
  • respondKeycloakLogin:
    • Signs JWT using BuildKeycloakJWTPayload with embedded Keycloak refresh token.
    • JSON response body remains clean without exposing the raw refresh token outside the JWT.

3. src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware/AuthMiddleware.go

  • In CheckAuth, extracts data["keycloak"] from validated JWT and sets c.Locals("keycloak", data["keycloak"]).

4. src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakLogout.go

  • In LogoutKeycloak, replaces manual body/query extraction with ExtractKeycloakRefreshToken(c, requestBody.RefreshToken, requestBody.Token).
  • If refresh_token was in the JWT, hasKeycloakToken is true and LogoutKeycloakSession is automatically executed.

5. Unit Tests Added

  • src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers_test.go:
    • TestBuildKeycloakJWTPayload: Verifies JWT payload with and without refresh token.
    • TestExtractRefreshTokenFromClaim: Verifies map, string, nil, and empty string handling.
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakLogout_test.go:
    • TestLogoutKeycloak_Handler_ExtractRefreshTokenFromJWT: Tests end-to-end logout with only Authorization: Bearer <Panorra JWT with keycloak claim> and verifies Keycloak session termination.
    • TestLogoutKeycloak_Handler_ExtractRefreshTokenFromBodyToken: Tests extraction from body {"token": "<Panorra JWT>"}.
  • src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware/AuthMiddleware_test.go:
    • TestCheckAuth_KeycloakClaim: Verifies c.Locals("keycloak") is populated from JWT.

Verification

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Auth/...
go test -v ./src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware/...
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Auth ./src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware
go test ./...
  • All 26 unit tests in src/Action/V1/Auth passed.
  • All unit tests in src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware passed.
  • go vet reported zero issues.
  • Entire project test suite across all packages passed cleanly.

Frontend (FE) Integration Guide

Summary for Frontend Developers

Previously, the frontend had to manually persist Keycloak's refresh_token in localStorage and send it back in the request body upon logout.
With this update:

  1. On Login: The frontend passes refresh_token along with access_token to POST /auth/keycloak.
  2. After Login: The frontend no longer needs to persist kc_refresh_token separately in localStorage. Only the standard Panorra JWT token needs to be stored.
  3. On Logout: The frontend simply calls POST /auth/logout with Authorization: Bearer <panorra_token> and an empty body {}. The backend automatically extracts the refresh token from the JWT and terminates the Keycloak SSO session.

1. Update on Login Endpoint (POST /auth/keycloak)

Include the refresh_token received from the Keycloak SDK / token response:

// Example when logging in with keycloak-js
const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/auth/keycloak`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    access_token: keycloak.token,
    refresh_token: keycloak.refreshToken, // <-- ADD THIS
  }),
});

const result = await response.json();
if (result.statusCode === 200) {
  // Store Panorra token as usual
  localStorage.setItem('panorra_token', result.data.token);

  // NO LONGER NEEDED:
  // localStorage.setItem('kc_refresh_token', ...);
}

2. Update on Logout Endpoint (POST /auth/logout)

When logging out, the frontend no longer needs to retrieve or send refresh_token in the body:

// Simplified Frontend logout function
export async function logout(): Promise<void> {
  const panorraToken = localStorage.getItem('panorra_token');

  try {
    // Simply call POST /auth/logout with the Authorization header
    await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/auth/logout`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        ...(panorraToken ? { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${panorraToken}` } : {}),
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({}), // Empty body: backend automatically extracts refresh_token from JWT
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn('Backend logout failed, continuing with local cleanup:', error);
  } finally {
    // Clear local storage
    localStorage.removeItem('panorra_token');
    sessionStorage.clear();

    // Redirect to login page
    window.location.href = '/login';
  }
}

Backward Compatibility Note: If an existing frontend client still sends { "refresh_token": "..." } in the body or query parameter, the backend still supports it seamlessly (100% backward compatible).

Problem

When a user logs in via GoThru Keycloak SSO, the frontend previously had to track and persist the Keycloak refresh_token separately in localStorage in order to pass it to the /auth/logout or /auth/keycloak/logout endpoint. If the client did not explicitly send refresh_token in the logout request body or query, Keycloak's SSO session remained active on Keycloak's servers.

Scope

  1. Keycloak Login (LoginKeycloak / authenticateKeycloak / respondKeycloakLogin):
    • Accept refresh_token in keycloakLoginBody and query parameters.
    • Embed "keycloak": {"refresh_token": "<token>"} in the generated Hasura JWT payload.
    • Keep the JSON response body clean (refresh token is stored exclusively within the JWT token).
  2. Auth Middleware (AuthMiddleware.CheckAuth):
    • Extract data["keycloak"] from the validated JWT token and store in c.Locals("keycloak", data["keycloak"]).
  3. Keycloak Logout (LogoutKeycloak):
    • If refresh_token is not explicitly provided in request body or query, automatically extract it from:
      • c.Locals("keycloak")
      • Authorization: Bearer <Panorra JWT>
      • Request body "token" field if provided as a Panorra JWT.
    • Terminate the Keycloak SSO session using the extracted refresh token.
  4. Helpers & Tests:
    • BuildKeycloakJWTPayload and ExtractKeycloakRefreshToken helpers in src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers.go.
    • Comprehensive unit tests in src/Action/V1/Auth/helpers_test.go, src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakLogout_test.go, and src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware/AuthMiddleware_test.go.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% backward compatible: Clients that still pass refresh_token explicitly in request body/query continue to work seamlessly. Clients that only send Authorization: Bearer <token> now automatically have their Keycloak session terminated.

Acceptance Criteria

  • LoginKeycloak embeds keycloak refresh token claim into generated JWT.
  • AuthMiddleware stores keycloak claim in Fiber locals.
  • LogoutKeycloak extracts refresh_token from JWT claims when not provided in request body/query and calls Keycloak SSO logout.
  • All unit tests pass in src/Action/V1/Auth and src/Middleware/AuthMiddleware.
  • Full project test suite passes cleanly.
